newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Diesel up on India, trader buying.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Diesel up on India, trader buying.

text.p: The gas oil market rallied on Monday after India bought a hefty 870,000 tonnes of gas oil while a Singapore trader pushed its four-week buying spree to about five million barrels.
But trading sources said they expected the local trader's stamina to be exhausted by the end of this week. "He would be a very brave man to continue," one trader said.
But other traders noted that the market has often been proven wrong on its predictions about when the local trading firm would stop its purchases.
The local trader bought another 450,000 barrels of gas oil on Monday, pushing the high prices into the second half of April, which hit $28.00 per barrel for the first time.
The trader bought an April 16-20 cargo at $28.00 and an April 8-12 cargo at $28.60 fob basis from a European major. Another European major sold an 8-12 cargo at $28.50.
However, some traders noted that values for early April appeared to have softened marginally, as a deal was done on Friday at $28.70.
Traders said the local trader was encouraged by India's large purchase, which was higher than the most optimistic estimates talked late last week.
They said India would be able to absorb some of the arbitrage cargoes heading to Asia but noted that the rally would be seen only in the near term.
The huge volumes of cargoes from Russia and the MidEast, estimated at least at 800,000 tonnes, would prompt softer prices in the medium term, they said.
The jet fuel market was dead, traders said. Two offers for second-half April cargoes were seen at $27.05-$27.10, but met no bids.
"There is no interest at all on jet now," one trader said.
